chapters.title: The Silent Lake
chapters.focus: past perfect · passive · mixed / third conditional · should have

pages.text: Crystal Lake was said to have the clearest water in all the realms, yet when {hero} and {pet} arrived, it was grey and still. A fisherman explained that it had looked like that ever since Glimmerfin, the lake serpent, had stopped coming to the [[surface|the top of the water]]. “Without her song,” he sighed, “the water simply loses its colour.”

q.q: According to the fisherman, why had the lake turned grey?
options: Glimmerfin no longer sang at the surface.
Fishermen had polluted the water.
A storm had stirred up mud.
A page had fallen into the water.
q.explain: “Without her song… the water simply loses its colour.”

pages.text: {hero} borrowed a small boat and rowed out to the middle. Looking down, they could just make out a faint light far below. “If I could swim like a fish,” {hero} muttered, “I'd have that page by now.” {pet}, however, was staring at something else: a tangle of old fishing nets [[wrapped around|circling something tightly so it can't move]] a huge silver tail.

q.q: What did {pet} notice that {hero} had missed?
options: a tail caught in old nets
a light far below the boat
a fish that could swim to the page
the fisherman rowing after them
q.explain: {hero} was looking at the light; {pet} was “staring at something else”: the nets around a silver tail.

pages.text: It took them nearly an hour to cut the nets away. When the last knot was finally undone, Glimmerfin rose from the water, her scales flashing in the sun. “I had been [[trapped|caught and not able to escape]] for weeks,” she said. “Had you not come, I might never have sung again.” She opened her mouth, and there, resting on her tongue, was the fourth page.

q.q: “Had you not come” means…
options: If you hadn't come
Because you came late
Although you came
When you come again
q.explain: Inversion of the third conditional: Had you not come = If you hadn't come.

pages.text: That evening, Glimmerfin's song drifted across the lake, and the water slowly turned a brilliant blue again. The fisherman admitted that the nets might have been his. “I should have cleared them up years ago,” he said, looking [[ashamed|feeling bad about something wrong you did]]. He promised that the lake would be checked every week from then on.

q.q: How did the fisherman feel about the nets?
options: guilty that he hadn't removed them
angry that someone had left them
proud that he had freed Glimmerfin
worried the song would stop
q.explain: “I should have cleared them up years ago” — should have + past participle = regret about the past.

options: embarrassed and guilty
tired and bored
surprised and pleased
nervous and excited
final.explain: Ashamed = feeling bad (guilty, embarrassed) about something you did.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse That Forgot
chapters.focus: past perfect · passive · third conditional · should have

pages.text: A few days after the lake had turned blue again, Glimmerfin surfaced beside {hero}'s boat with an unusual request. On a tiny island at the far end of the lake stood a lighthouse whose lamp had been [[tended|looked after carefully]] by the same old keeper for forty years. Three nights earlier, however, the light had gone out, and no one had seen the keeper since.

q.q: What was worrying Glimmerfin?
options: The lighthouse lamp had gone dark.
The lake was turning grey again.
Her song had stopped working.
A boat had sunk on the rocks near the island.
q.explain: “Three nights earlier, however, the light had gone out.”

The lake “had turned blue again”. The problem was that “the light had gone out”.
Nothing suggests her song had stopped. The trouble was the dark lighthouse.
notes.A boat had sunk on the rocks near the is: No boat had sunk. The worry was that “the light had gone out”.

pages.text: When they reached the island, the lighthouse door was found to be unlocked. Inside, everything was spotless, but the oil lamp at the top was cold, and a note had been pinned to the wall: “Gone to visit my sister. Mog will look after the light.” {hero} frowned. Mog, it turned out, was a small grey cat, [[curled up|lying with the body in a round shape]] fast asleep on the steps.

q.q: Why had the light gone out?
options: The keeper had left the job to a sleepy cat.
Someone had broken in through the window at night.
The keeper had run out of lamp oil.
A storm had blown the lamp out.
q.explain: The note put Mog in charge, and Mog was “fast asleep on the steps”. A cat can't light a lamp!

notes.Someone had broken in through the window: The door was unlocked and everything was spotless, so there's no sign of a break-in.
The lamp was cold, but the story never says the oil had run out. The clue is who was left in charge.
There's no storm in this chapter. The keeper had “gone to visit my sister” and left Mog in charge.

pages.text: {hero} climbed the spiral stairs, polished the glass and relit the lamp. Within minutes a warm beam was sweeping across the water again. Not long afterwards, a rowing boat appeared out of the dusk, and an old man stepped onto the jetty, looking [[sheepish|embarrassed because you have done something silly]]. “I should have asked a person, not a cat,” he admitted. “If you hadn't come, the fishing boats would have been lost in the dark.”

q.q: “If you hadn't come, the fishing boats would have been lost” tells us that…
options: {hero} came, so the boats were safe.
{hero} came too late to save the boats.
the boats were lost before {hero} came.
{hero} will come again to save the boats.
q.explain: Third conditional: an imagined past. In real life {hero} DID come, so the boats were NOT lost.

The beam was shining again before the boats came out, so {hero} was in time.
“Would have been lost” is imagined, not real. The boats were never lost.
notes.{hero} will come again to save the boats: This sentence is about the past, not the future.

pages.text: The keeper explained that he had been so excited about his sister's birthday that he had simply forgotten Mog couldn't climb stairs, let alone light a lamp. He promised that from then on the lamp would be checked by two people every evening. Mog, meanwhile, was given a new [[title|a special name that shows someone's job]]: Official Lighthouse Cat, in charge of naps.

q.q: What is funny about Mog's new title?
options: It makes sleeping Mog's official job.
Mog will now be lighting the lamp every night.
Mog asked for the title himself.
The keeper gave it to Glimmerfin.
q.explain: “In charge of naps”: Mog's only job is the thing he already does best.

notes.Mog will now be lighting the lamp every: Two people will check the lamp now. Mog's job is “naps”.
Nothing says Mog asked. The keeper gave the title as a joke.
The title is for the cat: “Official Lighthouse Cat”.

options: a little embarrassed
very frightened
proud and pleased with himself
rather sleepy
final.explain: Sheepish = embarrassed because you've done something silly, like leaving a cat in charge of a lamp.

notes.very frightened: He wasn't scared. He knew he had made a silly mistake.
notes.proud and pleased with himself: The opposite: “I should have asked a person, not a cat.”
notes.rather sleepy: That's Mog! The keeper felt embarrassed, not sleepy.

chapters.title: The Night Mog Woke
chapters.focus: past perfect · passive · third conditional · should have

pages.text: A storm had been promised for Friday night, and Glimmerfin was [[uneasy|a bit worried and not calm]]. The lighthouse lamp had been checked by two keepers every evening since Mog's nap adventure, yet something still felt wrong. When {hero}'s boat reached the island, the beam was steady — but Mog was nowhere to be seen.

q.q: What had changed since the last visit?
options: Two people checked the lamp every evening.
The lake had turned grey again.
The keeper had given the lamp to Glimmerfin.
Mog had been made the only lamp-lighter.
q.explain: “The lighthouse lamp had been checked by two keepers every evening since Mog's nap adventure.”

The lake isn't the problem this time. The new rule is two keepers checking the lamp.
notes.The keeper had given the lamp to Glimmer: Glimmerfin asked for help; she wasn't given the lamp.
The opposite: two people check it now. Mog is Official Lighthouse Cat of naps.

pages.text: They found Mog at last behind a coil of rope, staring at a loose [[shutter|a wooden cover for a window]] that was banging in the rising wind. The shutter had been left unlatched that afternoon. “If someone had closed it properly,” the old keeper muttered, “we wouldn't be listening to that racket now.”

q.q: What does the keeper's “If someone had closed it…” tell us?
options: Nobody closed it, so it bangs now.
Someone closed it carefully, so the shutter is quiet.
The shutter will be closed tomorrow for the first time.
Mog closed the shutter before the wind started.
q.explain: Third conditional about the past: the closing did NOT happen, so the banging IS happening.

notes.Someone closed it carefully, so the shut: The shutter is banging, so it was not closed properly.
notes.The shutter will be closed tomorrow for: This sentence is about a missed past action, not a future plan.
notes.Mog closed the shutter before the wind s: Mog was staring at it, not closing it. It “had been left unlatched”.

pages.text: {hero} climbed up, [[latched|fastened shut with a small metal bar]] the shutter, and climbed down again. Not a moment too soon: the first hard rain arrived, and the lake turned wild. The lamp, safe behind its glass, kept sweeping the water. Fishing boats, guided by the beam, made it home.

q.q: Why were the fishing boats able to get home?
options: The lamp kept sweeping the water.
Mog swam out to guide them.
Glimmerfin sang the storm away.
The keeper rowed out to each boat.
q.explain: “The lamp, safe behind its glass, kept sweeping the water. Fishing boats, guided by the beam, made it home.”

Mog stayed on the island. The beam guided the boats.
Glimmerfin was uneasy, but the lamp — not a song — guided the boats.
The keeper stayed at the lighthouse. The beam guided the boats.

pages.text: Afterwards the keeper admitted he should have checked the shutters as carefully as the lamp. Mog, who had stayed awake for once, was given a second title: Storm Watcher (naps still allowed on sunny days). “If Mog hadn't stared at that shutter,” {hero} laughed, “we might never have noticed it.” Mog [[blinked|closed and opened the eyes quickly]] once, as if to say the praise was accepted.

q.q: What is funny about Mog's new second title?
options: Mog is praised, but naps stay allowed.
Mog must now light the lamp alone every single night.
Mog asked to be called captain of all the boats.
The title means Mog can never sleep again at all.
q.explain: “Storm Watcher (naps still allowed on sunny days)”: a serious job with a sleepy escape clause.

notes.Mog must now light the lamp alone every: Two keepers still check the lamp. Mog's titles are joke-jobs with nap rights.
notes.Mog asked to be called captain of all th: Mog didn't ask for captain. The keeper gave the title.
notes.The title means Mog can never sleep agai: The opposite: “naps still allowed on sunny days”.

options: fastened shut with a catch
painted a bright brand-new colour
opened wide to let the strong wind in
tied loosely with a long piece of rope
final.explain: Latched = fastened shut, which is what {hero} did to the banging shutter.

notes.painted a bright brand-new colour: Latching is about fastening, not painting.
notes.tied loosely with a long piece of rope: A latch is a bar or catch, not a loose rope.

chapters.title: Glimmerfin's Fog Bell
chapters.focus: past perfect · passive · third conditional · should have

pages.text: By Saturday morning the storm had passed, but a thick fog had been pulled across the lake like a grey blanket. The lamp had been cleaned overnight, yet boats still drifted too close to the rocks. Glimmerfin was [[anxious|worried and wanting help soon]], and Mog — Storm Watcher on duty — sat upright on the rail for once.

q.q: What new problem appeared after the storm?
options: a thick fog over the lake
a missing soft spoon in the bakery
a torn lantern in the forest
a quarrel about kite height
q.explain: “A thick fog had been pulled across the lake like a grey blanket.”

notes.a missing soft spoon in the bakery: The spoon is Crumb's story. Here the problem is fog.
notes.a torn lantern in the forest: The lantern was Pip's tale. Here the lake is foggy.
notes.a quarrel about kite height: Kite quarrels were at Cloud Castle. Here the fog hides the rocks.

pages.text: The old keeper admitted the fog bell had been left untested since spring. “If someone had rung it at dawn,” he muttered, “the first boats wouldn't have drifted so near.” {hero} climbed the tower. The bell rope had been [[frayed|worn thin and almost broken]] by weather, but it still held.

q.q: What does “If someone had rung it at dawn…” tell us?
options: Nobody rang it, so boats drifted near.
Someone rang it carefully, so all boats stayed far away.
The bell will be invented tomorrow for the first time.
Mog rang the bell before the fog arrived.
q.explain: Third conditional: the ringing did NOT happen, so the drifting DID happen.

notes.Someone rang it carefully, so all boats: Boats drifted near, so the dawn ringing did not happen.
notes.The bell will be invented tomorrow for t: This is about a missed past action, not a future invention.
notes.Mog rang the bell before the fog arrived: Mog was on the rail. The bell “had been left untested”.

pages.text: {hero} [[spliced|joined two ends of rope by weaving them together]] the rope, and together with Glimmerfin they rang the fog bell until the sound rolled across the water. Fishing boats, warned by the deep tone, turned wide of the rocks. The lamp's beam was soft in the fog, but the bell did the guiding. Mog blinked twice, as if keeping score.

q.q: How were the fishing boats warned?
options: by the deep tone of the fog bell
by Mog swimming out alone
by a picnic shout from the meadow
by Crumb's bakery bell in the village
q.explain: “Fishing boats, warned by the deep tone, turned wide of the rocks.”

notes.by Mog swimming out alone: Mog stayed on the rail. The bell warned the boats.
notes.by a picnic shout from the meadow: The meadow picnic isn't here. The fog bell warned them.
notes.by Crumb's bakery bell in the village: Crumb's bell is in Candy Village. The fog bell warned the boats.

pages.text: Afterwards the keeper said he should have checked the fog gear as carefully as the lamp and the shutters. Mog was offered a third title — Fog Listener — with naps still allowed whenever the sun returned. “If Mog hadn't sat up on that rail,” {hero} smiled, “we might have waited too long.” Glimmerfin [[exhaled|breathed out slowly]] at last, the grey lake already brightening at the edges.

q.q: What is gentle about Mog's new third title?
options: Naps stay allowed when the sun returns.
Mog must swim to every boat in every fog.
Mog asked to be captain of the keepers.
The title forbids Mog from ever blinking again.
q.explain: “Fog Listener — with naps still allowed whenever the sun returned.”

notes.Mog must swim to every boat in every fog: Mog stays on the island with joke-titles and nap rights.
Mog didn't ask for captain. The keeper offered the title.
notes.The title forbids Mog from ever blinking: Blinking is fine; naps are still allowed in the sun.

options: worn thin and almost broken
painted a bright new gold colour
tied into a perfect brand-new knot
soaked completely in cold lake water
final.explain: Frayed = worn thin — which is how the bell rope looked before {hero} spliced it.

notes.painted a bright new gold colour: Fraying is about wearing thin, not painting.
notes.tied into a perfect brand-new knot: The opposite of a perfect new knot.
notes.soaked completely in cold lake water: Wet isn't the same as frayed.

chapters.title: Mog the Fog Listener
chapters.focus: past perfect · passive · third conditional · should have

pages.text: By Sunday afternoon the fog had thinned, but soft grey ribbons still drifted over the rocks. The fog bell had been tested at dawn, yet Glimmerfin wanted a second pair of ears on the rail. Mog — newly titled Fog Listener — was [[stationed|placed on duty in one spot]] on the warmest post, naps delayed until the sun returned for good.

q.q: Where was Mog stationed?
options: on the warmest post on the rail
inside Crumb's tiny bakery oven
under Pip's oak with a blanket
at Lady Quillon's kite picnic
q.explain: “Mog… was stationed on the warmest post.”

notes.inside Crumb's tiny bakery oven: The bakery is Candy Village. Mog is on the lighthouse rail.
notes.under Pip's oak with a blanket: Blankets under the oak are Pip's tale. Mog is on the rail.
notes.at Lady Quillon's kite picnic: The picnic is Cloud Castle. Mog listens for fog on the rail.

pages.text: A fishing skiff had been guided wide of the rocks the day before, but its captain admitted the night lantern had been left dim. “If Mog hadn't twitched an ear at that first grey curl,” the keeper muttered, “we might have waited for the bell alone.” {hero} smiled; the twitch had been [[prompt|quick and on time]], almost professional.

q.q: What does “If Mog hadn't twitched an ear…” tell us?
options: Mog did twitch, so they didn't wait for the bell alone.
Mog slept through every grey curl and never twitched.
The fog bell will be invented tomorrow for the first time.
Crumb twitched an ear instead of Mog.
q.explain: Third conditional: the twitch DID happen, so waiting-alone did NOT.

notes.Mog slept through every grey curl and ne: The keeper is glad Mog twitched — the opposite of sleeping through.
notes.The fog bell will be invented tomorrow f: This is about a past ear-twitch, not inventing the bell tomorrow.
Mog is the Fog Listener. Crumb is in the bakery.

pages.text: Together they walked the shore. Driftwood had been stacked into a low seat for Mog, and a soft towel had been [[draped|hung loosely over something]] across it for sun naps between watches. Fishing boats, already warned once by the deep tone, tipped their hats toward the rail. Glimmerfin exhaled; the grey lake was brightening again.

q.q: What was the soft towel for?
options: sun naps between Mog's watches
painting Crumb's thank-you sign
wrapping a picnic cloudberry tart
mending a torn pink lantern
q.explain: “A soft towel had been draped across it for sun naps between watches.”

notes.painting Crumb's thank-you sign: The sign is Crumb's story. The towel is for Mog's naps.
notes.wrapping a picnic cloudberry tart: Cloudberry tarts are at Cloud Castle. The towel is for naps.
notes.mending a torn pink lantern: Lanterns were Pip's tale. The towel is for Mog's sun naps.

pages.text: Afterwards the keeper said they should have given Mog a proper title years ago, joke or not. Fog Listener stayed — with naps still allowed whenever the sun returned — and a second title was whispered for calm evenings: Rail Philosopher. “If the towel hadn't been soft,” {hero} laughed, “even a Fog Listener might have [[complained|said something was wrong or unfair]].” Mog blinked once, as if filing the joke for later.

q.q: What is gentle about Mog's titles?
options: Naps stay allowed when the sun returns.
Mog must swim to every boat in every fog.
Mog asked to captain the fishing fleet.
The titles forbid Mog from ever blinking.
q.explain: “Fog Listener stayed — with naps still allowed whenever the sun returned.”

notes.Mog must swim to every boat in every fog: Mog stays on the island with joke-titles and nap rights.
Mog didn't ask for captain. The keeper keeps the titles light.
notes.The titles forbid Mog from ever blinking: Blinking is fine; naps are still allowed in the sun.

options: quick and on time
painted a bright new gold colour
soaked completely in cold lake water
tied into a perfect brand-new knot
final.explain: Prompt = quick and on time — like Mog's professional ear-twitch.

notes.painted a bright new gold colour: Prompt is about timing, not paint.
notes.soaked completely in cold lake water: Wet isn't the same as prompt.
notes.tied into a perfect brand-new knot: A knot isn't what prompt means here.

chapters.title: The Rail Philosopher
chapters.focus: past perfect · passive · third conditional · should have

pages.text: By a calm Tuesday evening the fog had thinned to silver threads. The fog bell had been tested at dusk, yet Glimmerfin wanted quiet company on the rail. Mog — newly titled Rail Philosopher as well as Fog Listener — was [[perched|sitting up high in a steady spot]] on the warmest post, thinking slow thoughts between soft blinks.

q.q: Where was Mog perched?
options: on the warmest post on the rail
inside Crumb's tiny bakery oven
under Pip's oak with a blanket
at Lady Quillon's kite picnic
q.explain: “Mog… was perched on the warmest post.”

notes.inside Crumb's tiny bakery oven: The bakery is Candy Village. Mog is on the lighthouse rail.
notes.under Pip's oak with a blanket: Blankets under the oak are Pip's tale. Mog is on the rail.
notes.at Lady Quillon's kite picnic: The picnic is Cloud Castle. Mog philosophises on the rail.

pages.text: A fishing skiff had been waved safely past the rocks the day before, but its captain admitted the spare lantern had been left unlit. “If Mog hadn't blinked twice at that first silver thread,” the keeper muttered, “we might have trusted the clear sky alone.” {hero} smiled; the blink had been [[measured|careful and not rushed]], almost scholarly.

q.q: What does “If Mog hadn't blinked twice…” tell us?
options: Mog did blink, so they didn't trust the clear sky alone.
Mog slept through every silver thread and never blinked.
The fog bell will be invented tomorrow for the first time.
Crumb blinked twice instead of Mog.
q.explain: Third conditional: the blink DID happen, so trusting-the-clear-sky-alone did NOT.

notes.Mog slept through every silver thread an: The keeper is glad Mog blinked — the opposite of sleeping through.
notes.The fog bell will be invented tomorrow f: This is about a past blink, not inventing the bell tomorrow.
Mog is the Rail Philosopher. Crumb is in the bakery.

pages.text: Together they walked the shore. Driftwood had been stacked into a low seat for evening thoughts, and a soft towel had been [[smoothed|made flat and neat by gentle hands]] across it for calm naps between watches. Fishing boats, already warned once by the deep tone, tipped their hats toward the rail. Glimmerfin exhaled; the grey lake was brightening again.

q.q: What was the soft towel for?
options: calm naps between Mog's watches
painting Crumb's thank-you sign
wrapping a picnic cloudberry tart
mending a torn pink lantern
q.explain: “A soft towel had been smoothed across it for calm naps between watches.”

notes.painting Crumb's thank-you sign: The sign is Crumb's story. The towel is for Mog's calm naps.
notes.wrapping a picnic cloudberry tart: Cloudberry tarts are at Cloud Castle. The towel is for naps.
notes.mending a torn pink lantern: Lanterns were Pip's tale. The towel is for Mog's calm naps.

pages.text: Afterwards the keeper said they should have given Mog both titles years ago, joke or not. Rail Philosopher stayed beside Fog Listener — with naps still allowed whenever the sun returned — and a calm evening rule was whispered: think first, blink twice, then rest. “If the towel hadn't been soft,” {hero} laughed, “even a Rail Philosopher might have [[protested|said something was wrong or unfair]].” Mog blinked once, as if filing the joke under Evening Thoughts.

q.q: What is gentle about Mog's evening rule?
options: Think first, blink twice, then rest — with naps still allowed.
Mog must swim to every boat in every fog.
Mog asked to captain the fishing fleet.
The titles forbid Mog from ever blinking.
q.explain: “Rail Philosopher stayed… with naps still allowed” and the whispered calm evening rule.

notes.Mog must swim to every boat in every fog: Mog stays on the island with joke-titles, nap rights, and slow thoughts.
Mog didn't ask for captain. The keeper keeps the titles light.
notes.The titles forbid Mog from ever blinking: Blinking is fine; naps and thinking are still allowed.

options: careful and not rushed
painted a bright new gold colour
soaked completely in cold lake water
tied into a perfect brand-new knot
final.explain: Measured = careful and not rushed — like Mog's almost scholarly blink.

notes.painted a bright new gold colour: Measured is about careful timing, not paint.
notes.soaked completely in cold lake water: Wet isn't the same as measured.
notes.tied into a perfect brand-new knot: A knot isn't what measured means here.
